v.rationale: The three implementations are nearly the same: a FormRequest, a controller using `currentAccessToken()->delete()`, and a named limiter keyed by lowercased email plus IP. All test suites pass. The deciding issue is the "every client" requirement. Only impl-1 changes bootstrap/app.php so that a guest on DELETE /api/auth/token or GET /api/me who doesn't send Accept: application/json gets 401. In impl-2 and impl-3 those requests return a 500 (Route [login] not defined), which I confirmed with probes. impl-1 also tests this case. All three return a 500 when `email` is an array, because the limiter key is built before validation runs. Whitespace in the email doesn't get around the throttle, because TrimStrings normalises it. impl-3 ranks above impl-2: it has stronger tests (window reset with travel, describe blocks, exact messages) and passes `validated()` values instead of Stringable objects. One drawback is that impl-3 dropped the `email` rule, so a malformed email gets 401 instead of 422. impl-2 also uses a closure route for /me and puts RefreshDatabase in the test file instead of Pest.php.
